---
title: "Still at Home"
execute:
  echo: false
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)

# Read in downloaded Census data and tract boundaries
sarasota <- read_rds("sarasota.rds")
tracts <- read_rds("tracts.rds")

# 1. Total living with parents across Sarasota by age group
living_by_age <- sarasota |>
  filter(variable %in% c("B09021_012", "B09021_019", "B09021_026")) |>
  mutate(
    age_group = case_when(
      variable == "B09021_012" ~ "18–34",
      variable == "B09021_019" ~ "35–64",
      variable == "B09021_026" ~ "65+"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(age_group) |>
  summarize(total = sum(estimate, na.rm = TRUE))

# 2. Number and percentage of 18-34 year olds living at home by tract
young_adults <- sarasota |>
  filter(variable %in% c("B09021_008", "B09021_012")) |>
  select(GEOID, NAME, variable, estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = estimate) |>
  rename(total_18_34 = B09021_008, living_at_home = B09021_012) |>
  mutate(pct_at_home = 100 * (living_at_home / total_18_34))

# Calculate median number across tracts
median_count <- median(young_adults$living_at_home, na.rm = TRUE)

# 3. Volusia County data and tract boundaries
volusia <- read_rds("volusia.rds")
volusia_tracts <- read_rds("volusia_tracts.rds")

volusia_young_adults <- volusia |>
  filter(variable %in% c("B09021_008", "B09021_012")) |>
  select(GEOID, NAME, variable, estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = estimate) |>
  rename(total_18_34 = B09021_008, living_at_home = B09021_012) |>
  mutate(pct_at_home = 100 * (living_at_home / total_18_34))

# 4. Central Florida regional data and tract boundaries
cf_data <- read_rds("central_florida.rds")
cf_tracts <- read_rds("central_florida_tracts.rds")
cf_counties <- read_rds("central_florida_counties.rds")

cf_young_adults <- cf_data |>
  filter(variable %in% c("B09021_008", "B09021_012")) |>
  select(GEOID, NAME, variable, estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = estimate) |>
  rename(total_18_34 = B09021_008, living_at_home = B09021_012) |>
  mutate(pct_at_home = 100 * (living_at_home / total_18_34))

# 5. County comparison: Sarasota, Volusia, and Orange
county_comparison <- bind_rows(
  young_adults |>
    summarize(
      county = "Sarasota",
      total_18_34 = sum(total_18_34, na.rm = TRUE),
      living_at_home = sum(living_at_home, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
  volusia_young_adults |>
    summarize(
      county = "Volusia",
      total_18_34 = sum(total_18_34, na.rm = TRUE),
      living_at_home = sum(living_at_home, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
  cf_young_adults |>
    filter(str_detect(NAME, "Orange County")) |>
    summarize(
      county = "Orange",
      total_18_34 = sum(total_18_34, na.rm = TRUE),
      living_at_home = sum(living_at_home, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
) |>
  mutate(pct_at_home = 100 * (living_at_home / total_18_34))
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-age-brackets
#| warning: false

living_by_age |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age_group, y = total)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1d3557") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Adults Living with Parents by Age Group",
    subtitle = "Sarasota County, Florida",
    x = "Age group",
    y = "Number of people living with parents",
    caption = "Source: US Census Bureau 2018–2022 ACS"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-tract-counts
#| warning: false

young_adults |>
  ggplot(aes(x = living_at_home)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 50, color = "white", fill = "#1d3557") +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = median_count,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "#e63946",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of 18–34 Year Olds Living with Parents",
    subtitle = paste0("Red dashed line indicates county median per tract (", round(median_count), " people)"),
    x = "Number of young adults (18–34) living with parents per tract",
    y = "Number of tracts",
    caption = "Source: US Census Bureau 2018–2022 ACS"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-map
#| warning: false

# Coordinates for major Sarasota County cities to provide geographic context
major_cities <- tibble(
  city = c("Sarasota", "Venice", "North Port"),
  lon = c(-82.543, -82.430, -82.198),
  lat = c(27.339, 27.100, 27.058)
)

tracts |>
  left_join(young_adults, by = "GEOID") |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pct_at_home), color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = major_cities, aes(x = lon, y = lat), color = "black", size = 2) +
  geom_label(
    data = major_cities,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = city),
    vjust = -0.6,
    size = 3.5,
    fill = "white",
    alpha = 0.85,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1),
    option = "plasma",
    na.value = "grey90"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Geographic Patterns of Young Adults Living with Parents",
    subtitle = "Percentage of adults aged 18–34 living with parents by Sarasota County tract",
    fill = "Living with\nparents",
    caption = "Source: US Census Bureau 2018–2022 ACS"
  ) +
  theme_void()
```

## Comparing Sarasota, Volusia, and Orange Counties

```{r}
#| label: plot-county-comparison
#| warning: false

county_comparison |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(county, pct_at_home, .desc = TRUE), y = pct_at_home)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1d3557", width = 0.55) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(round(pct_at_home, 1), "%")),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 4,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1),
    limits = c(0, 50)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Percentage of Young Adults (18–34) Living with Parents",
    subtitle = "Comparing Sarasota, Volusia, and Orange Counties",
    x = "County",
    y = "Percentage living with parents",
    caption = "Source: US Census Bureau 2018–2022 ACS"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

Among these three counties, **Sarasota** has the highest share of young adults living with parents (**36.5%**), followed by **Volusia** (**34.2%**), while **Orange County** has the lowest (**32.5%**).

Several key factors likely drive these differences:

- **College Enrollment & Student Rentals:** Orange County is home to the University of Central Florida (UCF), which enrolls over 68,000 students. Many students and recent graduates live in dense student apartments, off-campus shared housing, and dorms around eastern Orlando as roommates rather than living at home with parents.
- **Housing Costs & Retiree-Heavy Demographics:** Sarasota is an affluent coastal county with a high median age and steep housing and rental prices. For young adults entering the local workforce, high cost of living makes independent renting significantly more challenging.
- **Urban Density vs. Suburban/Coastal Communities:** Orange County's dense urban core provides a broader inventory of multi-family apartments and starter rental units compared to the single-family and retirement-oriented neighborhoods common in Sarasota and Volusia.

## Why Does Osceola County Have the Highest Rate in the Region?

Across all of Central Florida, **Osceola County** stands out with nearly half (**47.9%**) of young adults living with parents—the highest rate in the region. 

Why is Osceola so high?

1. **Multigenerational Family Norms:** Osceola County has a majority Hispanic population (56.1%). In Hispanic cultures, multigenerational living and young adults remaining in the family home until marriage or financial stability is culturally valued and common.
2. **Tourism & Service-Sector Wages:** Much of Osceola's economy is tied to the hospitality and service industries supporting the Kissimmee and Walt Disney World corridor. Because these positions often pay entry-level wages while regional rent prices have surged, young workers are often financially priced out of independent living.
3. **Absence of a Large Residential University Influx:** Unlike Orange County, Osceola does not have a massive residential university drawing tens of thousands of independent young adult renters from outside the area.
